themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Infrastructure Surge
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints spiked to 4 complaints THIS WEEK—a 3100% surge vs. 0.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.72)—signaling rapid expansion of sidewalk/street dining that may be creating new safety, accessibility, or quality-of-life conflicts in Park Slope's commercial corridors.
evidence: 4 outdoor dining complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (8-week average)
3100% spike with z-score of 11.72 (statistically severe anomaly)
No prior trend: issue appears to be emerging, not long-running
reporting_angles: Survey restaurants and residents on 5th Avenue and Prospect Park West to understand what triggered new complaints (encroachment, noise, blocked access, seating placement)
Cross-reference with DOB permits: are new outdoor dining licenses or expansions on file for this week/last week?

themes_detail.label: Dead Animals and Public Health
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints surged to 8 THIS WEEK—a 611% spike vs. 1.1 weekly baseline—concentrated over the past 7 days, suggesting a potential wildlife or sanitation crisis that warrants immediate health department investigation.
evidence: 8 dead animal complaints filed LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Concentrated timing suggests acute event (disease outbreak, predator activity, or environmental contamination)
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health & Mental Hygiene: are they tracking disease or contamination in Park Slope? Any investigations opened?
Interview residents in the neighborhoods where complaints clustered: what species, locations, timeframe?

themes_detail.label: Dangling Street Signs & Public Safety
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints jumped to 5 LAST WEEK—a 1233% spike vs. 0.4 weekly baseline—indicating deteriorating street infrastructure that poses injury or visibility risks in a district already managing high traffic and pedestrian volume.
evidence: 5 dangling street sign complaints filed LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Reflects systemic maintenance gap consistent with ongoing infrastructure budget requests from community board
reporting_angles: Request 311 complaint details: which intersections are affected? Correlate with DOT maintenance records.
Tie to community board's standing request for water main inspection and street infrastructure upgrades—is this a broader maintenance crisis?

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees & Park Maintenance
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree complaints jumped to 7 LAST WEEK—a 331% spike vs. 1.6 weekly baseline—alongside a separate 540% spike in animal-in-park complaints, suggesting neglected park vegetation management that may be creating safety and ecosystem issues across Park Slope's green spaces.
evidence: 7 overgrown tree complaints filed LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Parallel spike: 4 animal-in-park complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% increase, z-score: 4.85)—suggests vegetation density driving wildlife activity
reporting_angles: Request NYC Parks maintenance records for Prospect Park and other district parks: trimming and inspection schedules for past 4 weeks
Interview park users: are overgrown branches blocking sightlines or pathways? Are residents seeing increased wildlife (raccoons, coyotes) due to dense cover?

themes_detail.label: Sewer System Complaints Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints spiked to 19 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 217% jump vs. 6.0 weekly baseline—indicating potential localized sewage or drainage issues; timing and concentration warrant investigation before weather worsens.
evidence: 19 sewer complaints filed 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 6.0 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Aligns with community board's standing budget request for water main inspection on specific street segments—suggests chronic system weakness
reporting_angles: Map the 19 complaints: are they concentrated on one block or spread across district? Request DEP inspection reports.
Interview affected residents: backups, odors, or reduced drainage during rain? Any recent construction or street work nearby?
